title: Gireumjang Sesame-Oil Salt Dip
shortDescription: Toasted sesame oil, fine salt, and freshly ground black pepper form a minimalist individual dipping sauce for simply seasoned grilled foods.
culturalContext: Gireumjang literally points to an oil-based sauce and commonly accompanies unseasoned Korean grilled meat. Some versions include only sesame oil and salt, while pepper and other details vary; this draft keeps the formula intentionally spare.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Measuring spoons or small digital scale

instructions.heading: Inspect the oil
instructions.action: Check the sesame-oil label, best-by date, storage directions, and aroma before measuring.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Oil smells clean and nutty, not paint-like, bitter, or rancid.
instructions.safetyNote: Sesame is a major allergen; do not use an unlabeled decanted oil for guests.

instructions.heading: Measure
instructions.action: Measure sesame oil into a clean dry bowl, then measure salt and optional pepper separately.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: No water or food debris enters the oil.
instructions.safetyNote: Use completely clean, dry tools to limit contamination and splatter near the grill.

instructions.heading: Combine
instructions.action: Stir the salt and optional pepper into the sesame oil for 15 seconds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Salt remains partly crystalline and evenly distributed at the bottom.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not add raw garlic or other fresh aromatics to stored oil without a separately reviewed safety plan.

instructions.heading: Portion
instructions.action: Divide immediately among clean individual dipping dishes, about 1 tablespoon per person.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Each dish has a shallow layer with visible salt crystals.
instructions.safetyNote: Individual portions prevent raw-meat tongs and used bites from contaminating the master batch.

instructions.heading: Stir during service
instructions.action: Invite diners to stir lightly before dipping because salt does not dissolve fully in oil.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: A few salt grains cling to each dipped cooked bite.
instructions.safetyNote: Dip only fully cooked food with clean eating utensils, never raw meat or raw-meat tongs.

instructions.heading: Discard served portions
instructions.action: At the end of service, discard all individual portions and wipe oil spills promptly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: No used table sauce is returned to storage.
instructions.safetyNote: Oil spills create a slip and fire-spread hazard; keep the sauce away from open flame and wipe spills promptly.

grillSetup: No grill is used to make the dip; place individual dishes outside the heat and raw-meat zones, away from open flame and grill edges.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains sesame. Use dedicated dishes and utensils, and keep the dip away from peanut, tree-nut, soy, and raw-meat cross-contact at the grill.

substitutions: No neutral-oil substitution preserves the named sesame-oil character.
Omit black pepper for the simplest two-ingredient version.
ingredientSourcing: Choose toasted sesame oil in an opaque or dark container and check the sesame allergen statement.
Buy quantities small enough to use while the aroma remains fresh.
makeAhead: Measure ingredients up to 1 day ahead but store oil in its original container and combine just before service.
storage: Discard served portions. If an untouched master mixture remains, refrigerate in a clean dark airtight container for up to 3 days, following the oil label; bring briefly to cool room temperature before stirring.
reheating: Do not heat; keep away from open flame.
leftovers: Never save sauce from individual dipping dishes. Retain only an untouched master portion that stayed clean and was refrigerated promptly.
servingSuggestions: Serve with simply seasoned cooked beef or pork
Use one shallow individual dish per diner

faq.question: Should the salt dissolve?
faq.answer: No. Salt is not soluble in oil, so a light stir before dipping redistributes the crystals.

faq.question: Can I add raw garlic?
faq.answer: Not to a stored oil mixture in this draft; fresh garlic-in-oil requires separate validated safety controls.
